findings: [BLOCKING] Finalized-attempt score rewrite (security, confirmed): a candidate can submit non-empty answers after Completion or Termination and replace the stored answers and score. Restore an atomic `status == 'In Progress'` guard inside the finalization transaction, and solve terminal answer freshness before the status transition rather than reopening the result.

[BLOCKING] Terminal answer acknowledgement gap (security, confirmed): the browser navigates after /submit regardless of HTTP/JSON success, so answers newer than the server draft can be lost. Keep a recoverable terminal-pending state that retries from local storage and navigates only after /submit returns {ok:true}. Must be paired with the duplicate guard so freshness does not become a post-result rewrite capability.

[BLOCKING] Devtools auto-termination (security, confirmed): `devtools_open` has a finite threshold and is omitted from UNCERTAIN_AI_TYPES, so it can auto_submit/terminate when automatic action is enabled and the human gate is disabled. Set its threshold to -1 and add it to the explicit never-terminal set so the human-review-only guarantee survives config changes.

[BLOCKING] Mutable precheck evidence (security, confirmed): /precheck checks ownership but not status, so an owner can replace identity/precheck evidence and reset identity_verified=0 after finalization. Status-gate the write and make accepted evidence immutable except through a privileged recheck; put the status/immutability predicate in the update so it cannot race finalization.

[BLOCKING] Discarded ear-review evidence (security, confirmed): ear-view frames are cleared in `finally` without persistence, the audio-output-device-label indicator is absent, and api_hr_attempt strips precheck_report so HR cannot read the stored result. Persist and expose size-bounded, HR-authorized, non-conclusive/non-terminal review evidence; reducing the feature to self-attestation requires an explicit design change.

[BLOCKING] Continuous-incident row fragmentation (security confirmed; behavior corroborates as the second-granularity de-dup boundary): repeats of a stable incident ID that land at/after the 4.5s cooldown create additional rows instead of extending the existing one (server dedup only applies while age is strictly below the threshold). Update the existing row whenever the stable incident ID is seen, or maintain a separate server last-seen recovery window; cover a cooldown-crossing repeat in DB-backed verification. (Behavior rated this low-impact/non-blocking, but security confirms evidence/duration fragmentation.)

[BLOCKING] Missing DB-backed verification (security confirmed; behavior corroborates as DB runtime verification deferred): migration idempotency rerun, ownership 403s, non-HR denials, transactional finalization, dedup, deadline, autosave, heartbeat source labels, and CSV export were not executed (no project venv, no MySQL in-env). Run two migration passes, owned/non-owned and non-HR authorization checks, concurrent/duplicate terminal submissions, terminal answer preservation, heartbeat labels, and cooldown-crossing dedup against disposable MySQL, plus `python -m pytest tests/test_violation_engine.py`, before sign-off.

[NON-BLOCKING] Client reload uses localStorage only (behavior, possible): restoreDraftSelections() reads localStorage, never the server draft_answers, so resuming on a different browser/device shows no prior selections. Score safety still holds via the /submit server-side draft fallback; wire the server draft into the render if cross-device resume UX is wanted.

[NON-BLOCKING] Autosave drops option letters beyond A-D (behavior, possible): /autosave keeps only values in ('A','B','C','D'), so an MCQ with more than four options would not persist those selections to the draft (the live /submit POST still captures them). Confirm no assessment uses >4 options, or widen the allowed set.

[NON-BLOCKING] warning_count semantics changed (behavior, likely): warning_count now increments once per distinct-incident warn rather than only on the first warning. Intended under the new engine; confirm the HR dashboard reading of warning_count expects a running count.
